Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's first innings! The umpires are back out and the English players are also on the field. Skipper, Rohit Sharma will open the innings alongside Yashasvi Jaiswal for India. Mark Wood, the lone seamer in the English side has the new ball in hand and is ready to steam in. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

As for India, the spinners did a fine job at various occasions but it was Jasprit Bumrah who broke through at a couple of vital times. Ravichandran Ashwin got two big wickets up top and one at the backend while Ravindra Jadeja and Axar Patel ran through the middle order. Jadeja did go for plenty later on but his three wickets were a good trade-off. A solid showing overall and India will feel they can easily go beyond this total given the inexperienced spin attack of the opposition. England though will come back out on the field and come hard at the Indian openers. Stick around as India's reply is up next and there are still 23 overs left on Day 1.

Wow, a fast and furious half an hour or so of the final session and India have managed to bundle England out for just 246 runs. England came in post-Tea being 215/8 but soon enough, the skipper Ben Stokes launched an all-out attack and brought up his Fifty and went beyond that as well. Mark Wood couldn't hang around for too long and was castled after which Stokes played a few more shots before being dismissed by a beauty from Bumrah. All in all, the English batters got start and partnerships brewed but they couldn't get that three-figure stand and have fallen short of the 250-run mark as well.

OUT! TIMBER! It's all over for England. They are all out for 246 on the first day after winning the toss and batting first. Jasprit Bumrah delivers a beauty to get rid of Ben Stokes. He bowls the ball up with pace and makes it move away very late. Ben Stokes steps down the track looking to make room and is bamboozled by the late swing on the ball, completely playing all over it. The ball rushes on to hit the top of the middle stump and Jasprit Bumrah finishes things in style with a smile on his face.

In the second half of the session, there were a lot of things going on as Jasprit Bumrah picked up a wicket in his second spell but then came a bit of counter-punch from England. It was the debutant Tom Hartley who took on the spinners and notched up crucial runs before Jadeja cleaned him up. Ben Stokes sensed the occasion and opened up his arms, putting the ball away for a few crucial boundaries. Jadeja got three wickets in the session but was a bit expensive towards the end of the session as well. England will be eyeing up the 250-run mark from here whereas India will look to pick up the remaining two wickets quickly after the interval. Join us in about 15 minutes for the final session on Day 1.

Session summary - 31 overs, 107 runs and 5 wickets. India dominant in the second session but Ben Stokes has kept his side in it. Joe Root and Jonny Bairstow took to the crease for the Lunch break and were well-set on the crease but soon after, Bairstow got out and Root soon followed suit as Ravindra Jadeja and Axar Patel made their mark with the ball. Stokes and Ben Foakes had to rebuild again for England and seemed to be doing a decent job until Foakes too fell prey to spin as well.

A maiden to end and that will be Tea on Day 1! Ravindra Jadeja bowls a flighted ball on the off stump line and Mark Wood respects the ball by blocking it well and the Umpires say that its time for some Tea.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle as Rohit Sharma is seen leading the Indian side in a huddle before the players take their places on the field. Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley are the openers for England and the crowd is making a fair bit of noise already. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Three slips and a gully in place. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of this riveting contest but first the two sets of players lineup for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of England first followed by the Indian national anthem.

India's skipper, Rohit Sharma says they would have batted first as well and it looks dry but they have good experience on what needs to be done on such a track whether they bat first or bowl first. Adds that the guys are excited for a five-match Test series and a lot of them haven't played in a long series like this. Mentions that it is about backing yourself and making the best of opportunities. Informs that they have gone with three spinners and two pacers with Kuldeep Yadav missing out and Axar Patel gets the nod as he has grabbed onto his opportunities well.

Ben Stokes, the captain of England wins the toss and decides to bat first. He says that the wicket is going to start turning and more the time is spent it's going to get tougher to bat, so they want to bat first and put some good runs on the board. He adds by saying that they have opted for the playing 11 that suits the conditions and the combination that will make them win the games. Finishes by saying that Mark Wood is the only fast bowler playing for them in the playing 11 and they will be looking to use him the best way they can.
England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Ollie Pope, Joe Root, Jonny Bairstow, Ben Stokes (C), Ben Foakes (WK), Rehan Ahmed, Tom Hartley (On Test debut), Mark Wood, Jack Leach.
India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Shreyas Iyer, Ravindra Jadeja, KS Bharat (WK), Ravichandran Ashwin, Axar Patel, Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj.
TOSS - England win the toss and they will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Murali Kartik is pitchside and he is joined by Kevin Pietersen. Pietersen says it will be a fascinating series and adds that the pitch looks very dry around the popping crease on one side. Adds that this track will turn but how much it is going to spin remains to be seen. Mentions that the middle part of the surface has some grass covering but it is dry underneath. The final part of the wicket is a bit less dry and the team winning the toss will bat first.

England on the other hand haven't played Test cricket since the Ashes last year and it has been six months to that final game. They return to India after a woeful ODI World Cup but they have been a different side in red ball cricket off late. They will play aggressive cricket and will look to take the Indian spinners on but to what extent they succeed in doing so, that we will have to wait and watch. One frustrating loss for Ben Stokes was that young spinner Shoaib Bashir was sent back to England due to unresolved visa issues but he did receive his Indian visa, not in time to play in the first Test though. England have already announced their Playing XI and have one debutant in the side. Which of the two stalwarts will make their mark early in the series and start off on the right foot? We shall find out in due course. Toss and team sheets in a bit. Stay tuned.

India come into this series on the back of a pretty decent series up against South Africa away from home where the bowlers shined but there were issues with the bat. With no Virat Kohli for the first two Tests, a lot will depend on the openers and Shubman Gill will have to step up his game at number 3. The middle order looks decent but the bowling attack does look very potent especially in these conditions and they have four quality spinners to choose from to go along with the likes of Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj.

Hello and a very warm welcome to one and all. The highly anticipated Test series between India and England is here as the Anthony de Mello Trophy begins in Hyderabad with the 1st Test match. With crucial ICC WTC points on offer, expect this five-match series to be an entertaining affair.
